headline: Sales growth speeds up and margins widen
summary_short: Fastenal reported Q3 2026 net sales of $2,463M (+15.5% y/y) with operating margin of 21.5% (+90bp) and diluted EPS of $0.35 versus $0.29 a year ago.
summary_long: Daily sales rose 15.5% on share gains with larger customers, pricing of about 240 basis points and broad end-market demand. Gross margin slipped to 44.8% from 45.3% as customer mix and price/cost weighed, but SG&A fell 130 basis points as a share of sales, lifting operating margin to 21.5%. Operating cash flow was $422M, 105% of net income, as receivables grew with sales. Fastenal returned $328M through dividends and buybacks and carried $100M of debt. It expects 2026 net capex of $310–330M and trimmed its 2026 FASTBin/FASTVend signings goal to 27,000–29,000 units.
confidence_notes: The 8-K cover was resolved to the EX-99.1 earnings release. EPS delta uses the release's own stated change (+19.8%) from non-rounded values; the rounded $0.35 vs $0.29 would imply a slightly different percentage. The q/q EPS delta compares $0.35 with the shard's prior-quarter value of $0.33. Operating margin change of +90bp is as stated in the release. Guidance (net capex $310–330M; signings goal 27,000–29,000 MEUs, lowered from 28,000–30,000) is stated in the release but was not written to the event's guidance array because no sanctioned script exists for that write.

drivers.explanation: Results reflect strong daily sales growth, operating expense leverage and continued growth with larger customers supported by Onsite, digital and supply chain solutions.
Driven mainly by share gains with larger customers, pricing actions (about 240 basis points) and broad-based demand; manufacturing end markets grew 17.2% on a daily basis.
A shift toward larger customers cut margin about 50 basis points and price/cost cut it about 30 basis points, partly offset by sourcing savings, supplier rebates and tariff refunds.
SG&A leverage of 130 basis points more than offset the gross margin decline; employee and occupancy costs both improved as a share of sales.
Cash flow grew 9.0% but fell to 105% of net income from 115% as larger receivables and inventory absorbed cash with strong sales growth.
